result.topic_en: Calculations on integration by parts of $\varphi\cos\mu(x-a)$, an analysis of the extrema and zeros of $\sin x/x$ with a sketch of its graph, and estimates of sums of $(\sin n\alpha/n\alpha)^2$ and of a function $f(p/2n)$ expressed through $\varphi(\alpha)=\sum 1/(\alpha+z)^2$.
result.transcription:
$\varphi=(\mathfrak{C}+\mathfrak{C}'x+A_0\frac{xx}{2})\lambda(x)$ ; $\varphi'=(\mathfrak{C}+..)\lambda'+(\mathfrak{C}'+A_0x)\lambda$ ; $\varphi''=(\mathfrak{C}+..)\lambda''+2(\mathfrak{C}'+..)\lambda'+\mathfrak{C}'\lambda$
$\mu\mu\int\varphi\cos\mu(x-a).dx=\mu\{\varphi\sin\mu(x-a).[-dx-]-\int\varphi'\sin\mu(x-a)dx\}$
$=\mu\varphi\sin\mu(x-a)+\varphi'\cos\mu(x-a)-\int\varphi''\cos\mu(x-a)dx$

$f(x)=\frac{\sin x}{x}$ ; $f'(x)=\frac{x\cos x-\sin x}{x^2}=\frac{u}{x^2}$
$u=x\cos x-\sin x$ ; $u'=-x\sin x$ ; $u''=-x\cos x-\sin x$ ; $u'''=x\sin x-2\cos x$
[-$u$ ...-] $u_0=u_0'=u_0''=0$ ; $u_0'''=-2$
$f'(+0)=-$ ; $f'(-0)=+$ ; folglich $f(0)$ Maximum $=1$

$\cos x$ kann $=0$ sein ; $x=\mathrm{tg}\,x$
Maxima und Minima von $u$ nur für $x=m\pi$ ; $u'=0$ ; $u''=-m\pi.(-1)^m$
$u=(-1)^m m\pi$ ; $u'=0$ ; $u''=(-1)^{m+1}m\pi$
$\mathrm{tg}\,x=x$ für $x=0,\pm x_1,\pm x_2\dots$

$y=\frac{\sin x}{x}$, $y'=\frac{x\cos x-\sin x}{x^2}$
$y''=\frac{x^2(-x\sin x)-2x(x\cos x-\sin x)}{x^4}$
$=\frac{-x^2\sin x-2x\cos x+2\sin x}{x^3}$

[-$f(\frac{p}{2n})=(\frac{p}{2n})\frac{\varphi(2n)}{1^2}+(\frac{2p}{2n})\frac{\varphi(\frac{2n}{2})}{2^2}+\dots+(\frac{(2n-1)p}{2n})\varphi(\frac{2n}{2n-1})$-]
